prompt: How do I create a presentation template in PowerPoint?
completion:
## Creating a PowerPoint Template from Scratch (Windows & Mac)

A *template* is essentially a pre‑designed **Slide Master** that you can reuse for any number of new presentations.  
Below is a step‑by‑step guide that takes you from an empty file to a fully‑customized `.potx` (or `.potm` if you need macros) that you can drop into any new project.

---

### 1. Open a New Blank Presentation
- **Windows**: `File > New > Blank Presentation`  
- **Mac**: `File > New > Blank Presentation`

---

### 2. Switch to the Slide Master View

1. **Windows**: `View > Slide Master`  
2. **Mac**: `View > Master > Slide Master`

You’re now in the “master” editing mode where you can change the overall look that will propagate to every slide layout.

---

### 3. Set the Global Theme (Color, Font, Effects)

| What to Do | How |
|------------|-----|
| **Color Scheme** | `Design > Variants > Colors > Customize Colors…` – pick or define the 12‑color set that represents your brand. |
| **Font Scheme** | `Design > Variants > Fonts > Customize Fonts…` – choose a heading font and a body font. |
| **Effects** | `Design > Variants > Effects` – decide on shadows, bevels, etc. |

These selections automatically update all slide layouts under the master.

---

### 4. Adjust the Slide Size (Optional)

If you’re targeting a particular aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9 for widescreen, 4:3 for older monitors):

1. `Design > Slide Size > Custom Slide Size…`  
2. Choose the dimension, then click **OK**.  
3. Pick **Ensure Fit** or **Maximize** based on your preference.

---

### 5. Customize the Default Slide Master

The **first slide** in the Slide Master hierarchy is the *default* layout (often called “Title Slide”). Edit it as you would any slide:

- **Add a Background**:  
  - Right‑click → **Format Background** → Choose solid, gradient, picture, pattern, or theme background.  
  - If you want a branded image, click **Insert Picture** → **Picture** → `Insert`.

- **Add Placeholders**:  
  - `Slide Master > Insert Placeholder` → Choose **Title**, **Text**, **Picture**, **Chart**, etc.  
  - Drag the placeholder to the desired location; resize as needed.  
  - Right‑click → **Edit Placeholder** → rename (e.g., “Slide Title”, “Content Box”).

- **Set Default Styles**:  
  - Select the placeholder → change font, size, color, alignment, etc.  
  - Those defaults will be inherited by every new slide that uses this layout.

- **Add Footer / Header** (optional):  
  - `Insert > Header & Footer` → tick **Slide number**, **Date and time**, **Footer text**.  
  - Click **Apply to All**.

---

### 6. Create Additional Slide Layouts

Below the main master, you’ll find **layout slides** (e.g., Title & Content, Two Content, Comparison, etc.). To create your own:

1. Right‑click on the last layout → **Insert Layout**.  
2. Name the layout (double‑click the layout title).  
3. Add placeholders or graphics the same way you did on the master.  
4. Customize the background or formatting for that specific layout.

These layouts can be used later when inserting a new slide in your presentation.

---

### 7. Add Master-Level Graphics (Optional)

If you want a watermark, logo, or a recurring design element on every slide:

- Insert the graphic on the **Slide Master** itself (the topmost slide).  
- Anchor it so it doesn’t shift: right‑click → **Position** → choose `Fixed` or lock aspect ratio.  

---

### 8. Test Your Layouts

Switch back to normal view (`View > Normal` or `Slide Sorter`) and create a few sample slides using each layout:

1. `Home > New Slide` → pick each layout you created.  
2. Verify placeholders, fonts, colors, background, and that content flows correctly.

---

### 9. Save as a Template

1. `File > Save As`  
2. Choose a location → **Save as type** →  
   - **PowerPoint Template (*.potx)** – no macros  
   - **PowerPoint Macro‑Enabled Template (*.potm)** – if you used VBA.  
3. Give it a meaningful name (e.g., `CompanyBrandTemplate.potx`).

---

### 10. Use Your Template in Future Presentations

- **Windows**: `File > New > Personal` → Your template appears under “Personal”.  
- **Mac**: `File > New from Template` → your custom template will show up.  

Alternatively, you can double‑click the `.potx` file and it will automatically create a new presentation based on that template.

---

## Quick‑Tips & Best Practices

| Tip | Why It Matters |
|-----|----------------|
| **Keep it simple** | A cluttered master makes every slide hard to read. |
| **Consistent branding** | Use the same color palette, fonts, and logo placement across all layouts. |
| **Use placeholders** | They enforce content structure and make editing easier. |
| **Avoid over‑formatting** | Leave room for the presenter’s creativity. |
| **Name layouts clearly** | e.g., “Title & 1-Column”, “Two-Column Comparison” – this speeds up slide creation. |
| **Include a “Notes” placeholder** | Encourage presenters to use the speaker notes area. |
| **Test on different screens** | Especially if you’re using custom slide sizes. |
| **Version control** | Keep a “draft” version if you plan to iterate on the template. |

---

## Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

```
1. New → Blank Presentation
2. View → Slide Master
3. Design > Variants > Colors / Fonts / Effects
4. Design > Slide Size (optional)
5. Edit master: background, placeholders, footer
6. Insert > Layout (create new layouts)
7. Test slides
8. File > Save As > .potx
9. Use: File > New > Personal / Double‑click .potx
```

---

### Need a Ready‑Made Starting Point?

If you don’t want to build from scratch, PowerPoint ships with dozens of templates.  
You can download additional templates from the Microsoft Office Templates site or sites like SlidesCarnival, Envato Elements, or Canva.

---

**That’s it!**  
You now have a fully functional, brand‑consistent PowerPoint template that will save you time and keep all your future presentations looking polished. Happy designing!
